session8.topic_text: HIVE: Hive Architecture and Data Models, Hive Query Language (HiveQL) and Data Processing. / PIG, products in the Hadoop ecosystem other products in the Hadoop ecosystem for unstructured data analytics
assumptions: No content brief existed for this date -- built directly from topics.txt's two bullets (Hive architecture/HiveQL, Pig + broader Hadoop ecosystem tools).

Session7 (09/15) already introduced Hive/Pig/HBase by name at a one-paragraph overview level as part of last week's ecosystem survey. This week goes deeper (architecture, data model, HiveQL, Pig Latin) rather than repeating that overview -- flagged since it's a judgment call about depth/overlap, not something topics.txt states explicitly.

PDF rendered with 'Liberation Sans' instead of the skill's literal 'Arial' instruction -- Arial itself isn't installed in this container and pulling in real Microsoft fonts (ttf-mscorefonts-installer) hit an unrelated broken apt dependency (update-notifier-common's postinst needs a python3-apt build that doesn't match this container's non-default python3 alternative). Liberation Sans is metric-compatible with Arial and visually near-identical; this is a one-time environment note, not expected to recur once fonts-liberation is installed (which this run did).
Deck's closing 'next week' teaser is deliberately generic ('scaling analytics beyond batch') -- topics.txt has no 09/29 entry yet, so no specific next topic was invented.

Rest-of-ecosystem tools (Sqoop, Flume, Oozie, ZooKeeper) were selected as the standard Hadoop-ecosystem set for 'other products for unstructured data analytics' per topics.txt's bullet -- topics.txt doesn't name specific tools, this is the content brief's best-effort interpretation.
session8.environment_notes: This run installed the full toolchain from scratch in a fresh container: python-pptx+lxml (pip), r-base+r-cran-rmarkdown (apt), pandoc+texlive-xetex+texlive-fonts-recommended (apt), plus fonts-liberation and poppler-utils (apt, for the Arial substitute and a visual PDF check). All succeeded. ttf-mscorefonts-installer was attempted (to get literal Arial) and failed due to an unrelated broken apt dependency chain in this container (python3-apt/apt_pkg mismatch against a non-standard python3 alternative) -- not pursued further since fonts-liberation resolved the actual rendering need.
